name: Oily Hair
description: Hair that produces excess oil, typically noticeable at the scalp and forehead. This type of hair can appear shiny or greasy.
hair_texture: Smooth and glossy but can become limp due to excess oil secretion.
porosity: High porosity, which means the hair cuticles are lifted or open, allowing for easy absorption of moisture and products.
characteristics: Prone to greasy roots and oily feel throughout the day
Can be more difficult to style due to oiliness
recommended_ingredients: Salicylic acid or sulfur for reducing sebum production
Vitamin C to brighten and control shine
Tea tree oil for its antimicrobial properties
ingredients_to_avoid: Heavy oils and butters that can weigh down the hair
Silicones, which can create a greasy buildup
Alcohol-based products that can dry out the scalp
washing_frequency: Every 1-2 days, depending on oil production.
oil_recommendation: Use lightweight and water-based products that do not add excess oils to the hair.

morning_routine.action: Apply a clay mask or oil-control product to the scalp
morning_routine.purpose: Absorb excess oil and control shine

night_routine.action: Wash hair with an oil-control shampoo, focusing on the roots
night_routine.purpose: Remove accumulated oils and dirt from the day

night_routine.action: Apply a lightweight leave-in conditioner if needed
night_routine.purpose: Condition the ends without adding weight to the scalp

weekly_care: Deep condition with a hydrating mask at least once a week, but avoid using heavy formulas.
heat_styling_recommendation: Use heat protectants and limit heat styling sessions to maintain the integrity of the hair cuticles.
lifestyle_tips: Avoid excessive sugar and dairy in your diet, which can exacerbate oil production
Regularly exfoliate the scalp to remove dead skin cells
foods_for_healthy_hair: Fruits high in vitamin C (oranges, strawberries)
Leafy greens for iron and folic acid
Lean proteins like chicken or fish
common_mistakes: Over-washing the hair to the point of stripping natural oils
Using heavy products that can exacerbate oiliness
Not managing scalp health with proper hygiene
do: Stay hydrated and maintain a balanced diet
dont: Skip washing your hair, as this can lead to even more oil production
Use products that are too heavy or greasy
Over-exfoliate the scalp, which can irritate it

seasonal_care.summer: Increase the frequency of washes and use lighter hair care products.
seasonal_care.winter: Continue with regular washing but switch to richer, nourishing products as needed.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Pay extra attention to keeping your scalp dry and clean.

compatible_hair_types: Combination Hair (oily at the top, normal or dry elsewhere)
expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist for personalized advice if you have persistent oily scalp issues.
Regularly use dry shampoo to absorb oil throughout the day.
